# package knx

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-otfp/protocols/knx"
```

Package knx fingerprints KNXnet/IP (KNX Standard 03.08.02 Core and 03.08.03 Device Management) over UDP and TCP.

Detection sends one DESCRIPTION\_REQUEST (0x0203) to the control endpoint. Its HPAI is the "route back" address 0.0.0.0:0, which tells the server to answer the address the request came from, so the answer survives NAT; over UDP a second request with the HPAI of the local socket follows when the first draws nothing (servers that do not implement route back, reached without NAT). Over TCP route back is the only form the standard allows.

Only a strict DESCRIPTION\_RESPONSE (0x0204) matches: header length 6, protocol version 0x10, a total length equal to the datagram or frame, a DEVICE\_INFO DIB of 54 octets, a SUPP\_SVC\_FAMILIES DIB of family/version pairs, and further DIBs that exactly fill the body. An echo of the request is a DESCRIPTION\_REQUEST, not a response, and does not match.

The response carries the full identity, so detect and identify modes send the same request: KNX medium, individual address, project/installation ID, serial number, routing multicast address, MAC address, friendly name, the supported service families and their versions, KNXnet/IP Secure and Tunnelling v2 presence. Nothing that opens a connection or changes state (CONNECT\_REQUEST, tunnelling, group writes) is ever sent.
